picks.reasoning: Zeka in the mid lane is the best individual player on this Summoner's Rift, and in a one-game Swiss match that matters more than anything else. HLE also come in from the stronger region, which is a big edge here, and TES have no star who can answer him. I'm not buying any hype about TES scrapping back from behind. You can't count on comebacks when the other team has the better players.

Tempo is everything, and HLE are the team that actually plays the first fifteen minutes like they own the map. Kanavi sets the pace, Zeka is rolling on mid priority, and they're grabbing first tower and dragon way more often than TES. TES love to fight early for blood but can't turn it into objectives, and that's a recipe for getting out-tempoed. The LCK vs LPL gap is a big factor and it points to HLE too, though TES's scrappy comeback habit keeps this from being a lock.

Draft is where this game gets decided, and HLE walk in with the deeper, more flexible book: Zeka can play Orianna or Syndra, and they have enough jungle and top options to stay comfortable once Fearless starts taking champions away. TES lean hard on Ryze, Olaf and Renekton, and once those get picked or banned they have to improvise on the biggest stage. Add a clear gap between the regions, and I'm taking Zeka and HLE to out-draft them and carry the mid-game.

The numbers point one way here, and I don't lean this hard often. HLE have gone 6-1 outside their own region, while TES are 0-2 and haven't yet shown they can carry the LPL's form onto an international stage. Zeka's steady mid play gives HLE a safer floor, and TES's habit of falling behind and needing a miracle comeback is a risky plan in a single game.
picks.thinking: I'm leaning toward HLE given the flagged region gap favoring LCK over LPL, plus HLE's stronger overall record and their dominant cross-region performance compared to TES. That puts my confidence around 70%.

picks.reasoning: I'm backing HLE because this team has the feel of a locker room that believes in itself. They've bounced back from heartbreak, they've lifted a trophy this year, and Zeka plays with the calm of someone who knows where he fits. TES has real fight in them and I love their never-say-die spirit, but they've been wobbling lately and the international stage hasn't been kind to them, so I trust HLE's steadier mood and chemistry to win it.
